raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Only `HfRenderer` copied and pooled its tokenizer, so other renderers backed by a `TokenizersBackend` (e.g. Cohere, Inkling, KimiK3) used the tokenizer returned by `cached_get_tokenizer` directly. With `--renderer-num-workers > 1`, the render executor calls into the same Rust tokenizer concurrently and raises `RuntimeError: Already borrowed`.

Move both steps into `BaseRenderer.__init__`:

- Copy the tokenizer before `create_processor` so the cached instance is never mutated by the multimodal processor.
- Build the thread-safe pool as the last step of `__init__`, after the processor is created: the pool snapshots the tokenizer into deep copies, so mutations performed later would not reach those copies.

`HfRenderer` keeps its early copy (it registers the prompt-embeds placeholder token before `super().__init__()`) and marks itself with `_tokenizer_copied_by_subclass` so the tokenizer is copied only once. Its now-redundant pool call is removed.


fix: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/64034

🚀

@zhangxyai Are you already working on regression coverage for this PR? I’m looking into a small CPU-only reproducer using a real fast tokenizer through a non-HfRenderer’s public async path. I haven’t established a reliable failing baseline yet, but would be happy to coordinate on that and contribute tests alongside the revised design, if useful.

The key to reproduction is to set different input and output lengths during testing. For example, when using vllm bench serve, you need to configure --random-range-ratio 0.5. I don't have a GPU environment for thorough testing on my side—I only completed testing on a customized TPU. You are welcome to optimize and verify based on this work.

@zhangxyai Thanks for the reproduction hint. I investigated a CPU-only reproducer through `KimiK3Renderer.tokenize_prompt_async`, using real renderer/config constructors and a small in-memory fast tokenizer. Varying per-request truncation lengths exposed a dependency-version difference:

| Transformers / tokenizers | Unpatched base `9e0bc7a651` | PR head `e5b1bfdb8a` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 5.15.0 / 0.22.2 | 20/20 runs fail with `Already borrowed` | 20/20 pass |
| 5.20.2 / 0.23.2 | 20/20 pass | 20/20 pass |

The older pair is below this PR base's supported dependency floors. Its requirements specify `transformers >=5.16.1,<5.21.0` and `tokenizers >=0.23.2`; the CPU lock pins 5.20.2 / 0.23.2.

A separate Rust-tokenizer-only probe, holding the script and Python version fixed, produced 30/40 borrow errors on tokenizers 0.22.2 and zero on 0.23.2. The [v0.23.2 binding](https://github.com/huggingface/tokenizers/blob/v0.23.2/bindings/python/src/tokenizer.rs#L484-L528) uses `Arc<RwLock<Tokenizer>>`, with read locks for encoding and write locks for truncation changes.

Could you confirm the exact tokenizers version in the original customized environment, and whether the failure still reproduces with the currently supported dependencies? I have kept the candidate test as an experiment, but do not yet have a failing supported-version baseline suitable for a regression test on current main.
@Ondre119 My previous tokenizers version was 0.22.2, and it works after upgrading to 0.23.2. Thanks.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

I think we should avoid introducing subclass specific behavior in the base implementation. Perhaps it's better to introduce a separate function `get_threadsafe_tokenizer` and implement for each tokenizer type?

cc @noooop
